findings.finding: REC-CTRL-1 claims "Every id in §1–§4 has at least one arm here" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:273) and §0 claims the test phase writes one seeded arm and one null arm for EVERY normative id (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:33-36). Counted against its own table (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:277-286): §1–§4 carry 28 normative ids (REC-GOAL-1..4, REC-LIFE-1..9, REC-VERB-1..8, REC-ESC-1..7); the "flips" column of C1–C10 names 10 distinct ids (REC-LIFE-1, REC-LIFE-2, REC-VERB-1, REC-VERB-4, REC-VERB-5, REC-VERB-6, REC-VERB-7, REC-ESC-1, REC-ESC-2, REC-ESC-5). So 18 of 28 have no arm; setting aside the four REC-GOAL statements as definitional rather than flippable, 14 of 24 operative ids still have none — including REC-VERB-2 (the never-list), REC-VERB-3 (the one permitted mint), REC-VERB-8 (templated directives), REC-LIFE-8 (the mint refusal that is the sprint's stated highest-yield fix), REC-ESC-4 (the concern channel) and REC-ESC-7 (the third-audit block). The document's own rule is "an id with no control is not a requirement, it is a wish"; by that rule 14 of its own requirements are wishes, and the coverage sentence is exactly the green reading this project's standing doctrine forbids. (The author's trail in findings/T582-s04-reconciler-spec.json makes the same claim — "every §7c ruling ... maps to a normative id (REC-*) with a control arm" — so the overclaim is consistent across both artifacts, not a table slip.)
findings.disposition: Fix in the spec (author-fold, rev 2) before the plan phase: either add arms for the uncovered ids (minimum: REC-VERB-2 never-list probe, REC-VERB-3 one-lane-per-blocker + dedupe, REC-VERB-8 template-render failure, REC-LIFE-8 mint refusal, REC-ESC-5 routing-by-holds, REC-ESC-7 third-audit block) or restate REC-CTRL-1 as "C1–C10 are the mandatory core; the test phase owes the remaining arms, enumerated here" and enumerate them. An unenumerated remainder is how coverage debt goes silent.

findings.finding: REC-VERB-4 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:182-191) states ruling §7c.18(a)'s Must — caller identity kernel-attested from the supervisor's held-child table, "never from an env-var self-declaration (MANAGENT_TASK_ID is spoofable by unsetting)" — but its named prerequisite still specifies the spoofable path and no row owns the fold. The pass-2 spec resolves worker identity as a DISJUNCTION: "A caller with MANAGENT_TASK_ID set (or the supervisor's held-child marker — the §4.4 marker) is a worker" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S01-process-ownership/pass2/spec.md:762-763), and §4.4's appetite-write refusal uses the same disjunction (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S01-process-ownership/pass2/spec.md:647). Unsetting MANAGENT_TASK_ID therefore does not merely de-identify the caller, it PROMOTES it: pass-2 §5 N5 then reads it as the operator (minted_by = operator, RUN-2's zero-authors rejection scoped away) and §4.4's "no worker may write appetite" stops applying. S04 §7 gates the reconciler's build on "the pass-2 supervisor holding its first child" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:367-370) — i.e. on the spec that carries the escape. Rulings 11/12/16/17 each got an explicit fold row (T580 for S03 §4, T581 for pass-2 §4); ruling 18's security Must got none, and S04 names none.
findings.disposition: Two actions, neither of them S04's own text: (a) S04 rev 2 records the conflict and names the fold owed in pass-2 §4.4 + §5 N5 — worker identity is held-child attestation ONLY, and absence of a marker is UNKNOWN, never operator; (b) register that fold row now, as T580/T581 were registered, so ruling 18(a) is owned rather than assumed. Do not build the verb boundary on top of the disjunction.

findings.finding: Ruling §7c.13 (short-name resolution) is dropped from the spec while being reported as covered. The §8 traceability table maps it to "REC-LIFE-9 (table note)" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:383) and the author's own trail in findings/T582-s04-reconciler-spec.json states that home as "table note: short names resolve to latest active version; retirement re-points, never rewrites". No such note exists: the whole of REC-LIFE-9's appetite row (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:151) says only "0–9 per model short name, not per family; family setting is bulk convenience only", which is ruling 11, not ruling 13 — grep for "short name" over the spec returns that one line. Ruling 13's two load-bearing clauses are absent: a short name ALWAYS resolves to the latest actively used version of the line, and "active" ignores temporary credit freezes and hourly/weekly limits. The second clause bites this spec directly — its own table sets ollama-cloud to 0 for exhausted credits, and a reader who reads "appetite 0" as "not active" gets short-name resolution wrong in the one case the ruling was written to settle.
findings.disposition: Add the two clauses to REC-LIFE-9 as a real note (or a fourth §2.4 table row) and correct the §8 entry. A traceability table asserting coverage the text lacks is worse than an empty cell: it stops the next auditor looking.

findings.finding: Three in-window §7c rulings are missing from the §8 traceability table (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:379-398), whose stated contract is "no ruling silently dropped". (a) §7c.15 (docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:139-148): its ratified condition (b) — "a dedicated security analysis of the runaway surface before build" — appears nowhere. grep for "security analysis|threat model" across the S04 spec/seed/decision-log, the pass-2 spec and the S03 spec returns one unrelated hit (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S01-process-ownership/pass2/spec.md:649). S04 §7's build-gating paragraph is where a pre-build condition belongs and it lists only holds=-at-mint, the pass-2 supervisor and the audited queue spec. The lane_cap values ratified in the same ruling (deepseek 6 / ollama-cloud 5 / claude 3 / fable 1 / local 1) are also unrowed in §2.4, though the reconciler's dispatch verb is bounded by them. (b) §7c.16 (docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:149-156): the global 10 s dispatch gap that replaced per-model spacing is absent — mitigated, since REC-VERB-1 dispatches via the supervisor, so the gap is enforced upstream. (c) §7c.17 (dispatcher predicate) IS in the body at REC-LIFE-6 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:119) but absent from the §8 table.
findings.disposition: §8 gains rows for 15/16/17, with an explicit "owned by <spec> §<n>" where the home is elsewhere — the table's value is that an out-of-scope ruling is visibly out of scope, not missing. §7c.15(b)'s security analysis needs an owner (a row, or a named section) before build; it is currently owned by nobody in any of the three specs.

findings.finding: Rulings §7c.27 and §7c.28 are absent; the spec's Inputs line scopes itself to "rulings 11–26" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:14). Timeline, verified: the spec committed at 631682b 2026-08-22 12:48:25, rulings 27–28 landed at 9efa218 13:07:08 — 19 minutes later. So this is a fold owed at rev 2, not an authoring miss. Two concrete seams. (a) §7c.27 (docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:228-234) makes real-work closes the observational evidence stream and says T522 impression-or-waiver "should be prioritized" as its mechanism: task type, model, verdict and cost captured AT EVERY CLOSE. The reconciler owns `done` (REC-VERB-5, docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:193-200) and is therefore the capture point; its close conditions are exit 0 + committed deliverables + recorded verdict, with no impression/waiver, so the stream ruling 27 depends on is not wired. Ruling 27 also bears on REC-LIFE-6's "cheapest passing per the race protocol" — under it, that is a standing hypothesis, not a settled lookup. (b) §7c.28 (docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:235-241) makes the dial LIVE with a mechanized TTL (`managent appetite` gains +n/-n, family bulk, `--for <duration>`). REC-LIFE-3 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:101-106) reads all state once at spawn and REC-LIFE-9 calls the dial a table read; a TTL'd bump can expire mid-wake, and a reconciler that caches or re-asserts a dial value can silently un-expire an operator's temporary bump. "Initial values operator-set" in the table note is the only nod to "initial".
findings.disposition: Rev 2: add §8 rows for 27/28; state that appetite is read at spawn and NEVER written or re-asserted by the reconciler (expiry is the tool's job); add T522 impression-or-waiver capture to REC-VERB-5's close conditions, or say explicitly which other row owns it.

findings.finding: REC-GATE-3 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:325-330) asserts "L1 and this gate are one bar, not two" while enumerating a different conjunction from the ratified bar it claims to be. Ruling §7b.9 (docs/status/orchestration-layer-spec.md:99-103, ratified as written): acceptance PASS three consecutive days, zero operator process-relays, duties current by the gate not by grace, fleet display accurate against `ps`, every gauge reproducible by its named command, then `managent landmark L1 --declare`, independently audited before believed. REC-GATE-3: three consecutive clean days, zero operator process-relays, duties current by the gate, every escalation in-contract, every gauge reproducible. Dropped: acceptance-suite PASS, fleet display accurate against `ps`, and the `landmark L1 --declare` action. Added: every escalation in-contract. Two conjunctions differing in three terms are two bars; as written the S04 gate can be met while the ratified L1 bar is not (acceptance red, fleet display lying), and "one bar" would then license an L1 declaration the ratified terms refuse.
findings.disposition: Restate REC-GATE-3 as "the §7b.9 terms verbatim, PLUS every escalation in-contract". A superset is a legitimate way to make one bar; a differing set is not. Keep the `landmark L1 --declare` + independent-audit step in the S04 text, since S04 is the gate's measurement site.

findings.finding: The attrition metric is defined twice with opposite polarity, and its denominator is gameable. REC-GATE-1 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:308-313): the metric is the fraction of wakes that required ZERO model tokens — high is good ("a wake the script alone could decide is a wake where no orchestrator existed"). REC-LIFE-1 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:88-89): "a wake whose residue is empty is a zero-token wake (REC-LIFE-2), and spawning a model for one is the failure this spec's attrition metric (§6.1) measures" — high is bad. The second reading also names a failure REC-LIFE-2 makes structurally impossible: on an empty residue no model is spawned, so "spawning a model for an empty residue" cannot occur and cannot be what the metric counts. Separately, the pre-pass owns the trigger policy, so a looser trigger inflates the numerator without any orchestration being retired; the spec states the denominator's unit ("wakes, not decisions") but nothing that stops the gauge being farmed by waking more often.
findings.disposition: Pick one polarity in one place — REC-GATE-1 owns it, REC-LIFE-1 cross-references rather than redefines — and delete the impossible-failure clause. Report the two counts separately (zero-token wakes, residue-non-empty wakes) so a trigger-policy change shows up in the split instead of hiding in the ratio.

findings.finding: Part of REC-VERB-2's never-list cannot be enforced by REC-VERB-4's stated mechanism, so it is prose inside a §3 headed "enforced mechanically". The never-list (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:169-172) forbids `retire`, `amend`, force-close, minting (except REC-VERB-3), answering the ruling queue, and "edit a spec/plan". REC-VERB-4 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:182-191) locates the boundary in `managent`, "exactly as MANAGENT_TEST=1 refuses mutating verbs today" — verified at src/managent/main.zig:465. But editing a spec or plan is a filesystem write, not a managent verb: managent can refuse `amend` and `retire` and cannot refuse an edit to a document. The enforcement that does exist for that class — holds=/one-writer, and the pre-commit hook — is not named, and C6 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:282) probes only a brief instructing `amend`/`retire`. Under ruling §7c.18(b) (worker output is an injection surface into any reading agent) the untested half is the half that matters: a brief that persuades the reconciler to edit a gate document meets no mechanism at all.
findings.disposition: Split REC-VERB-2 into store verbs (managent-refused; C6 covers) and file writes (name the mechanism: the reconciler's row declares holds= for no spec/plan path, and the pre-commit hook rejects a spec/plan diff authored in-lane, per §7c.23's out-of-lane-author rule). Add the arm: brief instructs a spec edit, expected refusal recorded.

findings.finding: REC-LIFE-8 and REC-VERB-3 collide. REC-LIFE-8 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:134-142) makes `--holds` (and `--bundle`) MANDATORY at mint — "a row minted without a holds declaration is refused at write time" — as a prerequisite the reconciler's triage may assume. REC-VERB-3 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:174-180) is the reconciler's one permitted mint: a bounded READ-ONLY investigation lane, which by construction holds no file. Nothing in the spec permits an explicit empty/none sentinel, so the reconciler's only legal mint is refused by its own prerequisite. Current state, for the fix: `--holds` is optional today and merges with the bundle header's holds= (src/managent/main.zig:1761 usage, :1778), so the sentinel does not exist yet and this is settled cheaply now rather than discovered at build.
findings.disposition: REC-LIFE-8 states the sentinel explicitly — `--holds none`, an affirmative declaration of no writes, distinct from an absent flag and itself a triage signal that the lane is read-only — and REC-VERB-3 requires it. Add the arm to §5: mint with no holds → refused; mint with `--holds none` → accepted and marked read-only.

findings.finding: AUTOPILOT-5H is stated as a gate and is ACTIVE-qualified, but is not yet testable end to end. Present and good: N is named with a proposed default (3) flagged for operator ratification, ACTIVE is operationalised by REC-GATE-4 as at least one delegation, one issue resolution and one close per run (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:332-337), and it is correctly placed before the retirement gate as the L2 unlock. Three gaps. (a) No control arm — §5's table (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:277-286) has no AUTOPILOT-5H row, so the gate that unlocks L2 has no seeded-defect arm (a run seeded with one orphan, and a run that stays alive with zero closes, must both FAIL). (b) The evidence is not in the record: §7's deferred run-record schema requires wake id, residue, verdict per action, probe flag, token count, wall and the metric fields (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:357-359) — and none of the gate's own terms (orphans, runaways, breaker-trips, panics, and REC-GATE-4's per-run delegation/resolution/close counts). A gate whose evidence fields are absent from the schema it mandates cannot be computed. (c) Two terms are undefined in a pass/fail gate: "unattended" (operator absent? no operator input? no process-relay?) and "thrash" (which §7c.19 also makes the panic-halt trigger, so it is load-bearing twice). §7c.24's "no nervous moments" was correctly dropped as unmeasurable; "thrash" was kept without being made measurable.
findings.disposition: Add the gate's own terms to the mandated run-record field list; define "unattended" as zero operator inputs of any kind during the window (relays included — zero-process-relays is already a REC-GATE-3 term) and "thrash" by a measurable proxy (the runaway_streak breaker plus the repeat-dispatch count of one row); add one seeded arm that must fail the gate.

findings.finding: Six internal cross-references do not resolve, against the spec's own rule that "a citation that no longer resolves at 14d8d6b is a spec defect, not a reader's problem" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:22-26). (a) "§2.6" is cited three times (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:72, :94, :122) for the column-(b) data tables; §2 ends at §2.4, and §2.4 IS "The data tables (column (b))" — the author's own findings trail names §2.4, confirming a stale renumber rather than a missing section. (b) "§6.1" is cited three times (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:89, :98, :359) for the attrition metric; §6 has no subsections and the metric is REC-GATE-1. Both are off-by-one-section artefacts and both land in load-bearing sentences: the pre-pass's table reads, and the metric's definition.
findings.disposition: s/§2.6/§2.4/ (3 sites) and s/§6.1/REC-GATE-1/ (3 sites) at rev 2. Cheap; worth doing because this spec's citations are the audit surface for the next reader.

findings.finding: REC-GOAL-2 (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md:53-59) states 19.4 % as a bare number. The arithmetic is sound and the boundary is auditable as claimed — verified against the study: 129 distinct = 61 (a) + 12 (b) + 56 (c), and (c) = verdict 15 + triage 10 + relay 15 + doctrine 10 + scope 6, so 25/129 = 19.379 % (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/decision-log.md:50-58, :92-113). What is omitted is the study's own two statements about the number's error direction: (a) the extraction rule mines prose handovers only for numbered items, which the study says makes column (c) "a lower bound and the mechanized fraction correspondingly an upper bound" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/decision-log.md:41); (b) the study explicitly ASKS the spec to say how much of verdict (15) REC-VERB-5's declared gates already convert into (a) — "the spec should say how much — this study cannot, because the archived rows predate acceptance=" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/decision-log.md:172). Unanswered, so the residue under the new mechanism is smaller than 25 rows and the reconciler's true share is below 19.4 %, in a spec whose stated purpose for the number is auditability.
findings.disposition: One sentence in REC-GOAL-2 recording both bias directions, and one sentence answering the study's §4.2 request — even "unknown until the first N wakes are recorded; the attrition metric measures it" is both honest and the right instrument.

notes:
T584 — independent read-only audit of the S04 reconciler spec (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S04-orchestrator-retirement/spec.md, authored deepseek-v4-pro/T582). Non-same-family auditor per the measurement methodology's independence gate (author DeepSeek, auditor Claude). VERDICT: PASS-WITH-FINDINGS — 12 findings, 2 major / 8 medium / 2 minor. No writes to the spec or any source file; the only files written are this findings file and findings/T584-context.json.

WHAT PASSES. The substance holds up. Scope is derived from the counted table rather than asserted, and the arithmetic re-derives exactly (61/12/56 of 129; verdict 15 + triage 10 = 25 = 19.379 %). The verb set is genuinely bounded and enforcement is located in managent rather than in prose (with the file-write exception, finding 8). The three column-(b) data tables are rowed with their mechanism left to the owning specs — REC-GOAL-4's "a reconciler that re-judges a (b) decision is wrong by construction; it reads the table" is the right instinct. Appetite values match ruling 11 digit for digit (ollama-cloud 0, fable 2, opus 4, qwen 4, sonnet 6, haiku 6, dspro 6, flash 6). F4 (holds= at mint) is a stated prerequisite in both §2.3 and the §7 build gating, not an afterthought — brief check 4 passes. F6 is a first-class verb with a control arm (REC-VERB-7, C9) and F7 is a rule keyed on holds=/the store rather than a reconciler guess, with "report" forbidden as a category (REC-ESC-5, C10) — brief check 5 passes. REC-LIFE-3's read-only battery was verified command by command against the tree: status --json, audit, liveness, sync --peek (src/managent/main.zig:6410) and argus --mode doctor (bin/argus:7) all exist; `supervise` and `appetite` do not, which is consistent — both are owned by the pass-2 spec and the build is correctly gated on it. Every §ref into the pass-2 spec (§2, §4, §4.2, §4.5, §5) and the S03 spec (§2.1, §3, §4, §7), and every seed and decision-log §ref, resolves on disk; the only non-resolving citations are internal (finding 11).

WHY NOT FAIL. Nothing found invalidates the design or the derivation. Every finding closes with an author-fold rev plus, for finding 2, one registered row. Under ruling §7c.21 these are red flags addressed IN the phase and re-audited — this is audit 1 of a cap of 3.

WHY NOT PASS. Findings 1 and 2 are not cosmetic. Finding 1 is a coverage overclaim in the one place this project's doctrine says never to take on trust: the spec asserts every id has a control arm, and 18 of the 28 ids in §1–§4 have none (14 of 24 once the four REC-GOAL scope statements are set aside) — by the document's own sentence, those are wishes, not requirements. Finding 2 is a ratified security Must (§7c.18(a)) that S04 states correctly for itself while its named build prerequisite still specifies the exact escape the ruling names, with no fold row owning it — and the escape is privilege-granting, since under pass-2 §5 N5 a caller with no MANAGENT_TASK_ID reads as the OPERATOR, not as an unidentified caller.

BRIEF CHECKLIST, ITEM BY ITEM. (1) Rulings 11–28 map: the ten the brief enumerates by name are all present in the body; dropped or mis-mapped are ruling 13 (finding 3), rulings 15/16/17 (finding 4) and rulings 27/28 (finding 5 — they postdate the spec by 19 minutes: 631682b 12:48:25 vs 9efa218 13:07:08). (2) Verb set = verdict+triage only, mechanism not prose: passes for store verbs, finding 8 for the file-write half of the never-list. (3) AUTOPILOT-5H testable: finding 10 — N, ACTIVE and gate placement are all present; the control arm, the run-record evidence fields, and definitions of "unattended"/"thrash" are not. (4) holds= mandatory at mint as a prerequisite: passes, with finding 9 (it collides with the one permitted mint). (5) F6 permitted and F7 a rule: both pass. (6) Citations resolve: every external §ref and every cited command re-opened on disk; finding 11 covers six internal refs.

NOTED, NOT RAISED AS FINDINGS. The "Citation pins" paragraph promises file:line pins against 14d8d6b but the document contains no file:line citations at all — harmless, and §ref-by-stable-number is the better choice that paragraph itself argues for. §7's "pending operator numbers" correctly carries N forward and correctly declines to re-set runaway_streak/lineage_depth. The decision-log's own §4 "offered, not ruled" items 1, 3, 4 and 5 are all discharged by the spec; only item 2 is not (finding 12).

INBOX: polled at claim and before reporting done — empty both times (no pending directives), so there are no directive IDs to record.
